text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - South Korea's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans from Continental Grain at 104.50 cents C and F over May CBOT futures, traders said. Shipment will be from the U.S. Gulf for February 26-March 12, or shipment from the U.S. Pacific Northwest will be for March 13-27.
CORN SALE - Algeria bought 30,000 tonnes of maize around $150.00 per tonne C and F, traders said. Shipment is slated for February. Traders said the maize would be U.S. or Argentine.
CORN SALE - A Chinese government grain trading compmay last week sold a 12,000-tonne cargo of corn to Malaysia for $152.00 C and F, traders said.

WHEAT SALE - Philippine flour millers bought a total of 16,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for February shipment. The sale comprised 13,000 tonnes of white wheat sold by Mitsubishi and 3,000 tonnes of spring wheat from Cargill.

BARLEY, WHEAT SALE - Cyprus bought 12,000 tonnes of European wheat and 25,000 of barley. The barley was sold by Tradigrain for $140.87 per tonne for shipment in February. The wheat was sold by Toepfer for shipment in March, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - Egypt has tendered for 110,000 tonnes of No. 2 or better U.S. or Australian hard wheat. One shipment of 55,000 tonnes is slated for shipment February 5 to 15, and 55,000 tonnes is set for shipment March 1 to 10. The tender closes January 27.
- India will tender for 50,000 tonnes of wheat by the end of March. The tender closes January 29.
- Jordan will tender on February 5 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat or equivalent origin for shipment by March 31, traders said. U.S. wheat would be under the GSM 102 program.
WHEAT TENDERS - News was awaited on a Moroccan tender for 15,000 tonnes of optional origin milling wheat. Shipment was set for February 25 through March 5.
- Results were awaited on Bangladesh's tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian or Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, traders said.
- Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the government said.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board's tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use. The offer was seen closing January 16.

BARLEY TENDERS - Turkey will tender on February 3 to export 150,000 tonnes of feed barley and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley, European grain traders said Friday. The barley is for shipment in February and March.
- Iran plans to tender on January 27 to import 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley, European grain traders said Friday. The barley is for shipment in April.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 13.

SOYBEAN TENDERS - South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp. invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybeans on January 29. Shipment of one 20,000 purchase will be for January 30 to February 18 from the U.S. Gulf or February 14-March 5 from the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Shipment of the other 20,000 tonnes will be from the U.S. Gulf between February 24 to March 15 or from PNW March 11-30.

SOYMEAL/RAPESEED TENDER - South Korea's KFA will tender for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal and 5,000 tonnes of rapemeal Tuesday. The shipment of 20,000 tonnes is for April 20 arrival, while the 20,000 soymeal and 5,000 rapemeal are for arrival April 20.
PALM STEARIN TENDER - Egypt's state Food Industries Company said it sought 10,000 tonnes of Malaysian or Indonesian palm stearin for March delivery. The tender will close 1000 GMT on February 12.
MARKET TALK - Thai palm oil refineries urged the government to cut import tariffs on crude palm oil to zero from 10 percent currently, an industry source said.
- Australia hoped to sell up to 200,000 tonnes of wheat a month to Iraq from April onward under Iraq's food-for-oil program, an official with the Australian Wheat Board said
